mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in UNRATE over three consecutive months signals labor market tightening, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 1% in INDPRO and RSAFS over two months indicates an acceleration in industrial production and retail sales, reflecting strengthening economic activity and higher earnings expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > +1% and RSAFS > +1% over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and RSAFS rise by >1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST below -5% for three consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and home-related consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of HOUST < -5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.3% over one month signals a tightening monetary policy with falling inflation, which typically supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > -0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: PAYEMS rising by at least 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust job creation, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when PAYEMS > +1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: No significant change in GDPC1 over three consecutive quarters (within ±0.5%) signals economic stagnation, which erodes earnings momentum and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of GDPC1 stagnation (±0.5% QoQ for three quarters).
